facts.text: I've had a headache on both sides, at my temples.
I have pain on the left side of my neck.
It's constant; it doesn't let up.
It spreads up to my left jaw and the area around my left ear.
It's centered on one spot on the left side of my neck.
It gets worse when I move my neck or press on the spot.
I haven't had any recent infection.
I haven't had any chiropractic manipulation.
Otherwise I don't have any medical problems.

findings.name: neck examination
findings.result: Pain localized over the left carotid bifurcation, worse with neck movement and palpation.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Within normal limits; white-cell count 7 g/L (reference 4–10 g/L).

findings.name: metabolic panel
findings.result: Electrolytes, glucose and renal function within normal limits.

findings.name: contrast-enhanced CT of the neck
findings.result: Soft-tissue thickening around the distal common carotid artery, the carotid bulb and the proximal internal carotid artery on the left; no abnormalities of the other supra-aortic vessels or the aortic arch.

findings.name: carotid Doppler ultrasonography
findings.result: Isoechoic thickened arterial wall at the left carotid bifurcation; peak systolic velocity 90 cm/s; normal intraluminal flow; no intimal dissection or aneurysm.

findings.name: MRI of the neck
findings.result: Eccentric soft-tissue thickening at the left carotid bifurcation with hypointense T1 signal and hyperintense T2 signal; no T1 wall hematoma on fat-saturated sequences; intense perivascular enhancement after contrast administration.

findings.name: autoimmune serology
findings.result: Negative, including anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) and antinuclear antibodies (ANA).

findings.name: abdominal MRI
findings.result: No vascular abnormality (no fibromuscular dysplasia, no vasculitis, and no stenosis).

aliases: transient perivascular inflammation of the carotid artery
gold.reasoning: 1. Large‐vessel arteritis was considered but deemed unlikely — “In large vessel arteritis (giant cell arteritis and Takayasu arteritis), the thickened arterial wall enhances intensively on MRI; however, this enhancement is generally associated with significant luminal stenosis and it is not limited to the carotid bifurcation.” 2. Fibromuscular dysplasia was ruled out — abdominal MRI showed “no vascular abnormality (no fibromuscular dysplasia, no vasculitis, and no stenosis).” 3. Arteriosclerosis was unlikely — “No pathology of the other supra‐aortic arteries or of the aortic cross was found.” 4. Aneurysm was excluded — “No intimal dissection or aneurysm was seen.” 5. Systemic vasculitis was ruled out — “negative immunological laboratory tests including anti‐neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) and antinuclear antibodies (ANA).”

x002: 'Normal' apart from the focal neck pain recorded in x001.

source_issues: White-cell count given as '7 g/L (reference, 4–10 g/L)'; the unit is presumably G/L (10^9/L). Kept as written.
s003 calls the physical examination normal although s002 reports pain on palpation over the left carotid bifurcation.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with 5 days of bitemporal headache and 24 hours of left neck pain (s001-s008 are this presentation and its workup).
s002 supports both patient facts (location, aggravation by movement and pressure) and the neck examination finding.
'Medical history was otherwise unremarkable' is written as 'chronic medical problems' absent: the trauma, infection and chiropractic denials are not history items.
